title: RSIFlow: Adaptive Self-Improvement Workflows with an Evolving Meta-Agent
subtitle: 随瓶颈选择改进路径，并让改进者积累经验
source_label: Huan Zhang, Mingju Chen et al. · arXiv:2610.21791v1 · 2026

summary.text: **核心问题：任务智能体变了，改进它的方法也应随之变化。** RSIFlow 根据当前瓶颈选择改模型、改框架或修成果，并把干预经验沉淀到元智能体中。
summary.quote: We formulate this challenge as dynamic work- flow adaptation in RSI, where adapting bottlenecks and evolving workflow orchestration must be con- sidered together. As illustrated in Fig. 1, self- improvement workflows must adapt to bottlenecks that vary with task requirements and the agent’s ca- pability state. Even within a fixed domain, success- ful updates can reshape these bottlenecks and alter the effectiveness of subsequent workflow orchestra- tion. Meanwhile, workflow orchestration is itself a capability that can improve through experience. Feedback from workflow execution supports the ac- cumulation and refinement of reusable knowledge for diagnosis, workflow selection, and execution. These processes form a feedback loop: task-level updates reshape improvement requirements, while workflow experience refines the orchestration capa- bility that guides subsequent updates. summary.quote: Component-Specific Self-Improvement. Many approaches to agent self-improvement optimize a single predefined component. STaR (Zelikman et al., 2022) improves model parameters by re- peatedly fine-tuning on self-generated rationales that yield correct answers. AFlow (Zhang et al., 2025) searches code-represented workflows, while Recursive Harness Self-Improvement (Lee et al., 2026) refines prompt-level harness specifications using pairwise feedback over revision histories. Related approaches include DSPy (Khattab et al., 2024) for language-model pipeline optimization, GEPA (Agrawal et al., 2026) for reflective prompt evolution, and ADAS (Hu et al., 2025) for meta- agent-guided search over agent programs. In con- trast, AlphaEvolve (Novikov et al., 2025) evolves candidate programs through execution-based evalu- ation, targeting task artifacts rather than the agent’s improvement procedure. Evidence-driven skill maintenance. The Meta- Agent integrates newly distilled skills S t and gen- eral principles P t into the existing library K t through four evidence-driven operations. Add in- troduces previously uncovered strategies with their applicability and source evidence. Supplement en- riches existing entries with new outcome evidence while preserving their guidance. Revise refines applicability conditions, guidance, or preservation requirements through linked successor versions. Merge consolidates overlapping or superseded en- tries while preserving accumulated evidence and provenance. These operations update the library as C t = S t ∪ P t , K t +1 = ( K t \ R t ) ∪ C + t . Add in- troduces previously uncovered strategies with their applicability and source evidence. Supplement en- riches existing entries with new outcome evidence while preserving their guidance. Revise refines applicability conditions, guidance, or preservation requirements through linked successor versions. RSIF LOW leads in 11 of 12 benchmark–backbone settings across code gener- ation, tool use, and search-QA. Its overall scores reach 51.21% with Qwen3-4B and 59.86% with Qwen3-8B, surpassing the strongest baseline by 6.06% and 3.86%, respectively. summary.quote: Limitations RSIFlow is primarily evaluated using Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B as Task-Agent backbones. This set- ting is particularly relevant to resource-constrained agent deployments, where adaptive workflow or- chestration enables targeted modifications to identi- fied bottleneck components, while Meta-Agent evo- lution further improves bottleneck diagnosis and orchestration capabilities. However, whether these benefits remain significant with larger backbone models and at cluster scale remains unexplored. Future work will extend the evaluation to larger- scale settings to assess the scalability of RSIFlow. RSIFlow couples the Task-Agent and Meta- Agent, evolving the Meta-Harness through reusable skills and general principles to improve workflow orchestration without updating the Meta-Agent’s model parameters. However, this process intro- duces additional computational overhead, while adopting a lower-cost Meta-Agent may compro- mise evolution gains. Future work will explore counterfactual analysis to identify Meta-Agent de- ficiencies, apply targeted local modifications, and investigate Meta-Agent parameter optimization to improve evolution efficiency and stability.
